thread:
lina: Cutting RC for billing-service (sha=9c4d2a7). Change window 2026-04-05 02:00-04:00 UTC. Need QA and sheriff for canary.

releng: RC created and artifacts pinned -> id=4977. Artifacts: billing-service:9c4d2a7. Command: `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env canary --percent 5 --kv-warm`

patrick: staging smoke mostly green but DB-migration check shows long lock on invoice table during local migration dry-run. pasted snippet below.

qa-bot: ```text
2026-04-04T21:10:12Z WARN migration lock wait=12s table=invoice step=add_index
2026-04-04T21:10:13Z INFO retrying migration step
```

lina: tagging @sheriff for rollback plan. Pre-approve rollback target: billing-service:b6e5d1a (last stable). Rollback cmd: `kubectl set image deploy/billing billing-service=b6e5d1a -n prod`

sheriff: oncall for window. Also confirm DB rollback plan: incremental migration guard in place; in worst case we run reversible down script and cut traffic. DB lead @patrick, coordinate with DBA.

patrick: the migration is additive (index), but the lock time grows with active writes. For production traffic, it could cross our safe 5s threshold. Options: (A) proceed with canary but throttle write-heavy routes via traffic-shim to old variant during ramp, (B) postpone migration and promote binary-only RC without migration, (C) rollback. Thoughts?

lina: prefer safe route B if binary-only deploy is possible (skip migration). Can we build RC without running migration? releng?

releng: release pipeline supports a "db-freeze" flag to cut RC without auto-running migration. We can promote binary-only build by skipping migration hook: `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env canary --skip-migrations` But that means the new code will run against old schema — ok for index-add but must avoid code paths that rely on the new index for queries. Confirmed by Patrick.

patrick: I can gate the new index usage behind a feature flag so binary-only is safe for the ramp. We'll flip the feature flag to off in prod pre-ramp. Plan: (1) promote binary-only to canary, (2) run smoke, (3) if good, promote to prod, (4) schedule migration in a low-write window later and enable feature flag after migration.

sheriff: approve plan. Pre-authorized rollback target remains. If DB lock > 5s observed during any step we abort and rollback.

lina: promoting to canary now with skip migrations and feature flag off. `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env canary --skip-migrations --feature-flag billing.new_index=false --percent 5`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Promotion started rc/4977 -> canary (5%). Note: migrations skipped. Feature flag billing.new_index set to false for this rollout. KV warm in progress.

qa-bot: canary smoke: API flows ok, write-heavy endpoint latency stable. No migration locks observed (since migrations skipped). Error rate unchanged.

patrick: running targeted DB dry-run against prod-like replica to exercise index path check. no issues so far.

lina: moving to prod ramp: `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env prod --stages 10,50,100 --feature-flag billing.new_index=false`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Prod ramp started -> stage 10%. Notifying oncall.

sheriff: watching for DB lock metrics (pg_locks avg_wait). Alert if avg_wait > 2s for 3min.

ops: alert triggered: pg_locks avg_wait=3.8s at 02:15 UTC during 10% stage. Ramp paused automatically.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Ramp paused at 10%. Reason: metric(pg_locks_avg_wait) breached threshold. Options: rollback, hold and reduce write load, or revert stage.

patrick: this is surprising since migrations skipped. Likely due to new code changing query plans that touch invoice table more aggressively. I can temporarily reduce routing to the new service for write-heavy endpoints using traffic-shim. Suggest: apply shim for write routes -> route to previous variant (b6e5d1a) for 100% of write traffic for 30m, then resume ramp.

lina: do it. Apply shim and continue if locks drop.

releng: applying traffic-shim: `/traffic shim add --service billing --route \"POST /v1/invoice\" --to-tag b6e5d1a --percent 100 --duration 30m`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Traffic shim applied for writes to b6e5d1a. Resuming promotion to next stage 50%.

sheriff: monitoring locks closely.

ops: pg_locks avg_wait dropped to 0.5s within 90s after shim. No 5xx spike.

lina: continuing ramp to 50% then 100%. `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env prod --resume --stages 50,100`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Stage 50% reached. Monitoring.

qa-bot: 15m at 50% stable. No DB lock regressions; error rates normal.

lina: promoting to 100%. `/deploy promote rc/4977 --env prod --stages 100`

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Promotion to 100% complete. Prod running billing-service:9c4d2a7 with billing.new_index=false. Traffic-shim remains active for writes (30m timer).

patrick: scheduling migration run in a low-write window next week with DBA present. We'll enable the feature flag after successful migration and validate metrics.

lina: release notes: "Billing-service: prep for invoice index; binary-only rollout with migration deferred; used traffic shim for write-heavy endpoints during ramp. No schema changes applied during release." link: https://redwood.internal/release/4977

sheriff: closing watch. Postmortem action: add integration test that simulates write-heavy workload against new query plans. Assign to @patrick.

lina: thanks all, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
